record.paper_title: Open Problems in Communication and Computation
record.original_question: What is a general theory of information flow in stochastic networks?

evidence.quote: What is the general theory of information flow in stochastic networks?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic network modeled as a directed (or undirected) graph G = (V, E) in which each node v ∈ V is an information source or sink (or relay) and each edge e ∈ E is a noisy communication channel described by a conditional probability transition kernel p_e(y|x) between input and output alphabets. A set of source processes {X_s : s ∈ S} with prescribed joint distribution is to be transmitted to a set of sinks, where each sink t ∈ T demands a specified subset of the sources. A coding scheme assigns, at each node and each time step, a (possibly random) function of past observations to be transmitted on outgoing edges; decoders at sinks produce estimates of demanded sources. The capacity region of the network is the closure of all rate tuples for which arbitrarily small probability of error is achievable.

Develop a general theory of information flow in such stochastic networks. Concretely, give a single-letter (or otherwise computable) characterization of the capacity region of an arbitrary multi-source, multi-sink stochastic network with noisy channels, statistically dependent sources, and arbitrary demand structure, identifying the fundamental limits on simultaneously achievable communication rates and the optimal coding strategies (including the role of network coding, cooperation, feedback, and source–channel separation) that attain them.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of a general theory of information flow in stochastic (noisy, multi-terminal) networks is a long-standing open problem in network information theory. While special cases such as noiseless networks with single-source multicast (Ahlswede–Cai–Li–Yeung network coding theorem) and certain Gaussian/deterministic relay networks (Avestimehr–Diggavi–Tse approximate capacity) are well understood, the general multi-source/multi-sink noisy network capacity remains unresolved; standard textbooks (El Gamal–Kim) and surveys explicitly list it as open.

status_evidence.title: Network Information Theory (El Gamal & Kim)
status_evidence.snippet: A comprehensive treatment of network information theory; general capacity of noisy networks remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference identifies the general network capacity problem as unresolved.
